u.Marzo de 2026 · Geopolítica · Occidente: March 2026 · Geopolitics · The West · International Order
u.\"No hay nada peor que combatir con alia: "There is only one thing worse than fighting with allies, and that is fighting without them."
u.Hay una imagen que define la semana en l: There is an image that defines the week in which this article was written. In Canberra, the president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, shakes hands with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese before the cameras of the world. Behind them, the Australian Parliament building. Eight years of negotiations concluded on 24 March 2026. [Government of Australia / European Commission, 24 Mar. 2026] The agreement eliminates tariffs on 98% of the value of Australian exports to the EU. The obvious headline is commercial. The real headline is another.
u.La Unión Europea y Australia no firmaron: The European Union and Australia did not sign a trade agreement. They signed a shared diagnosis of the state of the international order. And that diagnosis, expressed in the neutral language of tariffs and quotas, is more revealing than any declaration of principles: the historic allies of the United States have concluded, with the data in hand, that American policy is a risk to be managed, not an umbrella to shelter under.
u.Llamarlo antiamericanismo sería inexacto: To call it anti-Americanism would be inaccurate. To call it de-risking would be technical but insufficient. It is, in the most precise sense of the term, portfolio management. And the portfolio being rebalanced is not financial: it is geopolitical.
u.Tres semanas antes del apretón de manos: Three weeks before the handshake in Canberra, Emmanuel Macron stood in front of the nuclear submarine Le Téméraire at a base in Brittany and delivered the most important defence speech by a European leader since the end of the Cold War.
u.Los anuncios eran concretos y sin preced: The announcements were concrete and unprecedented: France will increase its nuclear arsenal for the first time since 1992. It will deploy nuclear-capable aircraft on allied soil — something it had never done before. It will integrate Germany, Poland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Greece, Sweden and Denmark into joint nuclear exercises. And, a detail analysts were slow to process, it will stop publishing the size of its arsenal. The transparency Paris had maintained for decades as a signal of nuclear responsibility now becomes a deliberate strategic ambiguity.
u.La frase que eligió Macron para titular: The phrase Macron chose to headline the speech was deliberately archaic, almost Napoleonic: "To be free, one must be feared. To be feared, one must be powerful." This is not the rhetoric of a president who trusts that his principal ally protects him. It is the rhetoric of someone who has concluded that he must protect himself.
u.El canciller alemán Friedrich Merz anunc: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz immediately announced the creation of a Franco-German nuclear coordination group. Poland declared that this guarantees that "no enemy will dare attack us". The European defence bloc that for decades was a theoretical project began to take shape in real time. CSIS called the speech "the most significant doctrinal shift in the history of the Fifth Republic". What Macron announced was not merely an expansion of the arsenal: it was the formalisation of a rupture in the security logic that had governed Europe since 1949, the assumption that Washington's nuclear guarantee was unconditional, permanent and independent of who occupied the White House.
u.Esa asunción ya no opera. Y los aliados: That assumption no longer operates. And European allies have decided, at different speeds and without formal coordination, that it is prudent to budget for it.
u.Lo que siguió al discurso de Macron no f: What followed Macron's speech was not an isolated reaction but the expression of a process that had been accelerating for months. Within ninety days, the European Union concluded or decisively advanced five strategic trade agreements. The speed is unprecedented in the history of European commercial diplomacy. But the speed is the least interesting fact. The pattern is more revealing.
u.El caso de Indonesia merece más atención: The Indonesian case deserves more attention than it has received. The CEPA agreement concluded in Bali on 23 September 2025, after nine years of negotiations and a WTO dispute over nickel restrictions that reached levels of high diplomatic tension, is the most ambitious trade treaty the EU has ever concluded with a Southeast Asian economy. Indonesia is the world's largest nickel producer: it controls more than a quarter of the global supply of a mineral indispensable to electric vehicle batteries. Until the CEPA was signed, 80% of the processing capacity for that nickel was in the hands of predominantly Chinese producers. The agreement opens for the first time a direct supply channel with a stable legal framework for European buyers, outside Beijing's circuit. It was not presented as a geopolitical move. It was, formally, a free trade agreement. The distinction matters less than it appears.
u.En enero, la UE y la India firmaron lo q: In January, the EU and India signed what Von der Leyen called, without false modesty, "the mother of all deals": the largest trade treaty the EU has ever concluded, creating a free trade area for two billion people. [European Commission, 27 Jan. 2026; CNBC, 27 Jan. 2026] India cuts tariffs on European cars from 110% to 10%. The EU gains preferential access for textiles, leather and jewellery. Bilateral trade of 136 billion dollars a year expands with a growth horizon no analyst quantified conservatively.
u.Y en marzo, Australia. Ocho años de nego: And in March, Australia. Eight years of negotiations that had repeatedly stalled — over beef, over wine, over sugar — were unblocked the moment both sides calculated that the cost of not signing exceeded that of committing. Australia gains guaranteed access for critical minerals to Europe. The EU gains lithium, manganese and aluminium outside the Chinese circuit. Von der Leyen put it without euphemism before Parliament in Canberra: "For Europe and Australia, managing the relationship with China well is a strategic imperative." [European Commission / Government of Australia, 24 Mar. 2026] The euphemism "managing well" carries more weight than its diplomatic courtesy suggests.
u.El patrón es evidente: Indonesia, India,: The pattern is evident: Indonesia, India, Australia, Mercosur signed and in ratification, Mexico, Canada deepening CETA. None of these agreements is with China. All share some combination of institutional stability, governance values and the critical minerals Europe needs for its energy and digital transition. This is no coincidence of scheduling. It is a doctrine without an official name.
u.El acuerdo UE-India incluye además, en s: The EU–India agreement also includes, in its chapter on digital trade and financial services, provisions oriented towards laying the foundations of interoperability between central bank digital payment systems — the digital euro and the digital rupee — as well as linking India's instant payment system (UPI) with Europe's (TIPS). It is one of the first times in the history of trade treaties that a financial architecture clause of this scope has been included, designed to facilitate direct transactions between the two economies with less dependence on the dollar as intermediary currency. [European Commission, financial services chapter of the India–EU FTA; fintech analysis: eij.news, Feb. 2026] Connally's phrase from 1971 — "the dollar is our currency, but your problem" — is finding, fifty-five years later, its answer in the form of financial plumbing. It is not rhetoric. It is infrastructure under construction.
u.Vale detenerse aquí para ser precisos so: It is worth pausing here to be precise about what is happening, because conceptual imprecision has generated more confusion than clarity in the public debate.
u.El de-risking no es decoupling. No es la: De-risking is not decoupling. It is not the total separation the West attempted, without success, with China in recent years. Nor is it anti-Americanism. The United States remains the principal buyer of European and Canadian exports, and the military umbrella no trade agreement can replace. NATO is not in question. Intelligence links are not in question. Access to American military technology is not in question.
u.Lo que sí está en cuestión —y lo que los: What is in question — and what the data of the last eighteen months suggest with growing clarity — is whether economic dependence on a single partner that has become less predictable is a risk worth managing or one worth continuing to ignore. The answer the EU and Canada are giving, through agreements rather than declarations, is the first.
u.La ironía es que la frase que el secreta: The irony is that the line Nixon's Treasury Secretary John Connally threw at his European allies in 1971 — "The dollar is our currency, but your problem" — has found its echo fifty-five years later, but with the roles partially reversed. Now it is the allies who, without saying it with that brutality, are beginning to make their own decisions about how much exposure to American volatility they are willing to absorb.
u.Los números sostienen esa lectura. El ín: The numbers support that reading. The dollar index fell approximately 11% in 2025 — the worst annual performance in decades — driven by tariff uncertainty and doubts about the Fed's independence. [Al Jazeera / Morgan Stanley, Jul. 2025] Moody's downgraded the US sovereign rating from Aaa to Aa1 in May 2025, citing persistent deficits and a growing interest burden — the first time the US had lost its last triple A rating. [Moody's, 16 May 2025; Fortune, 16 May 2025] Danish and Dutch pension funds reduced their Treasury positions, a discreet but technically significant move. The ECB converted its euro repo lines, until then emergency instruments, into permanent facilities available to all the world's central banks: a signal of strategic intent that is hard to misread. None of this implies that the dollar will lose its global reserve status in the short term. The depth of the American market, its liquidity and its legal infrastructure have no equivalent. But the direction of travel is clear.
u.Una pregunta relevante no es si estos mo: A relevant question is not whether these movements will survive Trump but whether they would survive his absence — and the answer suggested by the institutional architecture being built is that they would, because signed agreements create facts that electoral calendars do not erase so easily.
u.IV. Canadá dice adiós en voz muy baja: IV. Canada says goodbye very quietly
u.Ningún caso ilustra la magnitud del reor: No case illustrates the magnitude of the reordering under way more clearly than Canada's. Not because it is the most dramatic geopolitically — it is not. But because it is the most improbable.
u.Durante décadas, Canadá fue el aliado má: For decades, Canada was the most faithful, most silent and most dependent ally of the American system. Seventy-eight per cent of its exports went to the United States. Its security depended almost entirely on the NATO agreement. Its foreign policy followed, with discreet variations, Washington's agenda. It was the neighbour that never caused trouble.
u.En tres semanas de marzo de 2026, el pri: In three weeks of March 2026, Prime Minister Mark Carney did the following: he travelled to New Delhi and signed the CEPA with India — uranium, LNG, artificial intelligence, critical minerals, and a payments dialogue mechanism aimed at interoperability between India's UPI system and the Canadian financial system. He flew to Toronto to sign the modernisation of CETA with Brussels and launch negotiations for Canada's first digital trade agreement. He formally joined European defence's SAFE programme. He visited Australia to discuss a new Hanseatic League — an alliance of middle powers, Canada, Germany, the main EU partners, the United Kingdom, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand, which would represent 30% of global GDP.
u.\"Como el país más europeo entre los no: "As the most European country among the non-Europeans, Canada looks first to the European Union to build a better world", Carney said at the EU–Canada summit last June. He even went so far as to suggest Canada's participation in the Eurovision Song Contest, a detail that on its own sums up the distance that has opened in the relationship with Washington.
u.La meta declarada es reducir la dependen: The declared goal is to reduce commercial dependence on the United States from the current 78% to 50% within a decade. This is not a rhetorical aspiration. It is a public policy objective with a budget, institutions and signed agreements. In the economic history of recent decades, few American allies have undertaken so deliberate and accelerated a reconfiguration of their commercial architecture. Carney does not call it a rupture. He calls it diversification. The distinction is important and probably sincere: Canada neither can nor wants to break with its southern neighbour. What it is doing is building alternatives in case that neighbour continues to be unpredictable. The difference between rupture and diversification is the same as that between selling all risk assets and hedging with options. The underlying diagnosis of the asset is the same.
u.V. La UE que crece hacia dentro y hacia: V. The EU that grows inwards and outwards
u.Hay un elemento de este reordenamiento q: There is an element of this reordering that trade-focused analyses tend to undervalue: the simultaneous expansion of the European Union in both its dimensions, external and internal.
u.Hacia afuera, los cinco acuerdos en nove: Outwards, the five agreements in ninety days are the most visible expression. But there is an equally significant internal dimension: the EU is being sought out, actively and from multiple directions, by countries that until recently considered it a less attractive option than an alliance with the United States or alignment with Moscow.
u.Islandia votará el 29 de agosto en un re: Iceland will vote on 29 August in a referendum on whether to resume EU accession negotiations, suspended in 2013. The explicit trigger is Trump's tariffs and the threats over Greenland — Trump's nominee as ambassador to Reykjavik went so far as to joke that Iceland should be the 52nd state of the United States. Iceland's GDP per capita is the fifth highest in the world. It already applies all single market legislation through the EEA. It is already in Schengen. It already opened 27 of the 33 negotiating chapters between 2010 and 2013. Its accession, if the referendum enables it, could be completed in two years.
u.Armenia inició formalmente su proceso de: Armenia formally began its accession process in 2025, directly defying Russia. Montenegro closes negotiations this year with the aim of entry in 2028. Ukraine and Moldova are advancing. The EU is not only signing outwards: it is also actively sought from the post-Soviet east, the Atlantic north and the Balkans. All for different reasons but with the same underlying structural factor: the world of single dependence — on the United States, on Russia, on China, as the case may be — no longer looks safe.
u.Lo que emerge no es una superpotencia eu: What emerges is not a European superpower in the classical sense. It is something more modest and more durable: a bloc large enough and coherent enough to offer a credible alternative institutional, commercial and security anchor for countries that need options. The demand exists. The EU is, for all its internal dysfunctions, in a position to meet it.
u.China no emerge de este reordenamiento c: China does not emerge from this reordering as a counterweight. The decision by the EU, Australia and Canada to diversify towards India, Indonesia and the ASEAN markets is explicitly non-Chinese. Von der Leyen did not speak of China as an alternative partner in Canberra: she spoke of China as a shared risk. The EU–Australia agreement has at its centre access to critical minerals outside the Chinese processing circuit, which controls 80% of global capacity. The digital interoperability of the India agreement is a financial architecture designed to reduce the friction of the dollar as intermediary — not to replace it with Chinese infrastructure. De-risking is diversification, not the substitution of one hegemon for another.
u.Tampoco es la historia de una ruptura li: Nor is this the story of a clean break with Washington. The United States remains, by a considerable margin, the principal buyer of European and Canadian exports. Its capital market has no equivalent in depth or liquidity. Its military technology — from missile systems to satellite intelligence — remains indispensable to the defence doctrines of every country that signed agreements with the EU in recent months. The American nuclear umbrella, however much Macron complements it with French dissuasion avancée, remains the backbone of European deterrence against Russia. None of these movements occurs in a vacuum.
u.Lo que está cambiando no es el mapa de a: What is changing is not the map of alliances. It is the level of certainty with which those alliances can be taken for granted. For seventy-five years, the post-war international order functioned on a set of assumptions: that the United States was a predictable actor within the institutions it had created, that the dollar was the global reserve asset par excellence, that NATO was a permanent and non-negotiable commitment. Those assumptions have not disappeared. But their certainty has degraded enough for rational actors — governments, pension funds, central banks, trade negotiators — to have begun designing their strategies for a world in which they are no longer automatic. That is what is happening. And it is happening faster than most Washington-centred analyses have been willing to acknowledge.
